newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEAKER AGAINST UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEAKER AGAINST UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar took further pummelling from importer demand on Wednesday to close easier against hard currencies, dealers said.
"Today was a hectic day with record payments being made. I personally paid out U.S.$15 million," one dealer commented.

Dealers said the Reserve Bank, which had been standing on the sidelines since last week and watching as the local unit buckled under import pressure, had finally come into the market with a few pockets of foreign currency, but this had done little to appease demand.
"The central bank came in with a few dollars today, but they came in rather late and the money was too little to offset the market shortage," said a dealer.
"Maybe the dollar will stabilise towards the weekend," he added.

Dealers still maintained that the ongoing strike by civil servants demanding pay rises from government had not impacted the market, pointing to the fact that the currency could not be traded outside Zimbabwe and was therefore not likely to be moved much by foreign investor sentiment.

At Wednesday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar, which dipped to a low of 10.2200/3000 at one point before the central bank's intervention, was at 10.1900/2600 against the key U.S. unit. This compared with 10.1200/1500 overnight.
On the crosses, it fell to 15.9170/16.0370 against sterling from 15.7630/8180 and was also easier versus the mark at 6.9170/9690 compared to Tuesday's 6.8540/8770.
Against the rand it finished at 2.2660/2820 from 2.2350/2440 the previous day.
